artifacts.name: Density distribution
artifacts.summary: How markets density varies across neighbourhoods, as a Lorenz curve (Gini 0.57; 0 = perfectly even, 1 = all in one sub-area). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
The distribution of markets density (per km²) across the area’s administrative sub-areas, shown as a Lorenz curve (Gini 0.57; 0 = perfectly even, 1 = all in one sub-area). A long tail or low median points to many under-served neighbourhoods.

artifacts.name: Statistics

artifacts.description: Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: farmers_markets · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = -0.17. 1 hot-spot and 0 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of markets density (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 10 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over markets density: **High-High** = a dense neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a sparse one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: farmers_markets · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Provision vs population
artifacts.summary: Do markets track where people live? Markets per 1,000 inhabitants against each sub-area’s population. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is an administrative sub-area, plotting its population against its markets per 1,000 inhabitants. Sub-areas low on the vertical axis but high on the horizontal axis are under-served relative to their residents — an equity signal a density map cannot show.

artifacts.name: Provision per capita

artifacts.description:
Each administrative sub-area shaded by its number of markets per 1,000 inhabitants, so the colour reflects provision *relative to residents* rather than raw density. A populous sub-area with average density can still read as under-served here. Sub-areas without usable population data are omitted.

artifacts.description:
A kernel-smoothed density of markets: the point counts are blurred into a continuous surface so clusters show as smooth hot regions rather than individual grid cells — a boundary-free complement to the sub-area choropleth and the raw heatmap.

artifacts.name: Distance to nearest market
artifacts.summary: How far to the nearest market from anywhere in the area (metres). Darker = further. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area, each cell shaded by the straight-line distance to the nearest market. Dark cells are the furthest from any feature — the access gaps. Straight-line (not routed), so it is an optimistic lower bound; it needs no routing service.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: farmers_markets · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Data currentness
artifacts.summary: How recently each market was last edited in OpenStreetMap (median 2 yr ago). Darker = longer since the last edit. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is a feature, shaded by the number of years since its last OpenStreetMap edit (measured against the data snapshot). Clusters of dark points mark areas where the OSM picture is ageing and may warrant a re-survey — a spatial companion to the data-quality note.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: farmers_markets · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Availability on a Sunday afternoon
artifacts.summary: Opening hours are well mapped here (100% of managed venues). 0 markets are known to be open on a Sunday afternoon. "Not specified" mostly covers freely accessible open-air places carrying no opening hours.
artifacts.description:
Features classified by whether their OpenStreetMap opening_hours indicate they are open at a fixed reference time (a Sunday afternoon). Managed venues such as libraries and museums may be closed then; open-air places usually carry no opening hours and are counted as "not specified". This indicator is only shown where enough venues carry opening hours to be meaningful.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: farmers_markets · reachability: straight-line distance.
